outputs/teds/findings_rows.csv.0.main_caveat: Code 7 combines fentanyl, prescription opioids and buprenorphine (no fentanyl-specific code); admissions are treatment episodes at publicly funded facilities, not people or prevalence.
outputs/teds/findings_rows.csv.0.original_claim: TEDS-A (through 2023): heroin's share of primary-opioid admissions fell and 'other opiates & synthetics' rose, mainly from 2021.
outputs/teds/findings_rows.csv.0.supported_claim: From 2019 to 2024, heroin's share of primary-opioid admissions changed by -33.3 percentage points and the 'other opiates & synthetics' share by +33.4 points in the 35-state panel.
outputs/teds/findings_rows.csv.1.main_caveat: First-time admissions are not new cases of addiction (they also reflect access, capacity and time from onset to treatment). 2019 lies inside a 2018-2020 prior-treatment coding artifact driven by California; the coding-shift-excluded sensitivity addresses this.
outputs/teds/findings_rows.csv.1.original_claim: TEDS-A (through 2023): first-time primary-opioid admissions per 100k fell at ages 18-24.
outputs/teds/findings_rows.csv.1.supported_claim: First-time primary-opioid admissions per 100k people aged 18-24 changed by -53% from 2019 to 2024 (lower bound; -54% upper bound) in the 35-state panel, and by -43% without states flagged for prior-treatment coding shifts.
outputs/teds/findings_rows.csv.2.main_caveat: Admissions track treatment entry at publicly funded facilities (funding, capacity, 2020 disruption, office-based buprenorphine not captured); deaths are mostly illicitly made fentanyl.
outputs/teds/findings_rows.csv.2.original_claim: TEDS-A (through 2023): from 2019, opioid deaths rose relative to primary-opioid admissions.
outputs/teds/findings_rows.csv.2.supported_claim: From 2019 to 2024, opioid deaths changed by +12% and primary-opioid admissions by -39% in the 28-state deaths panel.
outputs/teds/findings_rows.csv.3.main_caveat: A single year; the 2024 TEDS-A file excludes South Carolina and Washington (neither is in the panel).
outputs/teds/findings_rows.csv.3.original_claim: (new) 2023 -> 2024, the first TEDS-A year overlapping the decline in overdose deaths.
outputs/teds/findings_rows.csv.3.supported_claim: From 2023 to 2024, opioid deaths changed by -32% and primary-opioid admissions by -7%; the opioid death rate fell relative to the admission rate.

outputs/teds/meta.json.coding_shift_rule: first-time share changes by more than 25% points year to year
outputs/teds/meta.json.completeness_rule: TEDS admissions in every year of the window and total admissions never change by more than 50% year to year (ratio within [0.5, 1.5])
outputs/teds/meta.json.method:
Phase 4b: TEDS-A treatment admissions as an independent, AREA-LEVEL signal on opioid addiction.

    python -m src.step_t            # harmonization check, panels, (a)-(d), coverage sims, ledger rows T1-T4

Admissions are not prevalence: they count treatment episodes (not people) at publicly funded facilities,
depend on funding, capacity and referral practice, and miss office-based buprenorphine. Never joined to
NSDUH. TEDS-A now runs through 2024 (combined 2006-2023 file + 2024 single-year file, identical codes),
so 2023 -> 2024 overlaps part of the decline in overdose deaths (which began in late 2022).
outputs/teds/meta.json.rules.T1: Heroin's share of primary-opioid admissions fell and 'other opiates & synthetics' rose 2019 -> end year: 'holds' if both share changes have 95% CIs excluding 0 in the main specification AND in the through-2023 specification AND both log-odds trends excluding 2020 have CIs excluding 0; 'partial' if the main specification meets this but a sensitivity does not; 'fails' otherwise.
outputs/teds/meta.json.rules.T2: First-time primary-opioid admissions per 100k aged 18-24 fell 2019 -> end year: 'holds' if the log change CI excludes 0 (negative) for both bounds (missing NOPRIOR as not first-time / first-time) in the main specification, the through-2023 specification and the coding-shift-excluded sensitivity; 'partial' if the main specification meets this but a sensitivity does not; 'fails' if the main CI includes 0.
outputs/teds/meta.json.rules.T3: From 2019, opioid deaths rose relative to primary-opioid admissions (d > 0): 'holds' if d's CI excludes 0 (positive) for start 2019 in the main and the through-2023 specifications; 'partial' if only one; 'fails' if neither.
outputs/teds/meta.json.rules.T4: 2023 -> 2024 (first overlap with the death decline), primary-opioid admissions vs opioid deaths: 'not distinguishable' if d's CI includes 0; otherwise 'holds' for the observed direction (d > 0: deaths rose relative to admissions; d < 0: deaths fell relative to admissions).
outputs/teds/meta.json.scope: TEDS-A now runs through 2024, so 2023 -> 2024 overlaps part of the decline in overdose deaths (late 2022 onward); earlier years describe treatment admissions before that decline.
outputs/teds/meta.json.source: TEDS-A (SAMHSA): combined 2006-2023 PUF (2015-2023) + 2024 single-year PUF; CDC VSRR state file (xkb8-kh2a) opioid deaths 'Opioids (T40.0-T40.4,T40.6)', Dec 12-month-ending; Census state population (intercensal 2015-2019, Vintage 2025 2020-2024)
